title: Two-fer
statement_markdown:
Two-fer or 2-fer is short for two for one. One for you and one for me.

Given a name, return a string with the message: `One for name, one for me.`

However, if the name is missing, return the string: `One for you, one for me.`

Implement `two_fer(name='you')` that takes an optional name.
hints: Use f-strings to format the result string easily.
Make use of Python's default arguments in function definitions.
explanation: By setting the default parameter `name='you'`, we can simply return an f-string `f"One for {name}, one for me."` which cleanly handles both cases.
reference_solution:
def two_fer(name: str = 'you') -> str:
    return f"One for {name}, one for me."
complexity: O(N) time and space where N is the length of the string.

sample_tests.expected: One for Alice, one for me.
